name: Checkbox
description: A box that people tick to turn one option on or off, or to pick any number of options from a set. Use a Switch instead when the change takes effect immediately.
summary: Tick one or more independent options

elements.name: Box
elements.description: The control: unchecked, checked or indeterminate

elements.name: Label
elements.description: Clickable text in a <label> that names the option

elements.name: Hint text
elements.description: Extra detail under the label, linked with aria-describedby

elements.name: Legend
elements.description: <legend> that asks the question for a group of checkboxes

elements.name: Error message
elements.description: Says what to do, such as "Select at least one topic"

variants.caption: Group stacked — options in a column under a legend
Group inline — short options in a row
With hints — a line of detail under each label

usageNotes: Use a Checkbox when each option stands alone and any combination is valid. When exactly one option must be chosen, use a Radio group.
Put related checkboxes in a <fieldset> whose <legend> asks the question. Each box still needs its own <label>.
Wrap the input in its <label> or link them with for, so clicking the text toggles the box. This also gives a larger target (WCAG 2.5.8).
Use the indeterminate state only for a parent box whose children are partly checked. It is set with script (indeterminate = true) and is not a submitted value.
An unchecked box sends nothing with the form. When agreement is required, use required and an error that says what to do, such as "Confirm that you agree to the terms".
htmlOutline:
<label>
  <input type="checkbox" name="terms" required>
  I agree to the terms
</label>
